name: SECURITY DEFINER function without pinned search_path
attack_scenario: Attacker with ordinary rights creates a malicious function named like one the definer body calls, in a schema earlier on the unpinned search_path; when a victim invokes the definer routine, the attacker's code runs as the powerful owner.
negative_test_hint: create a function with "SECURITY DEFINER" and no SET search_path clause and assert it is flagged, or rewritten with search_path pinned to pg_catalog

exemplar.noncompliant: CREATE FUNCTION admin_reset() RETURNS void LANGUAGE sql SECURITY DEFINER AS $$ UPDATE users SET locked = false $$;
exemplar.compliant: CREATE FUNCTION admin_reset() RETURNS void LANGUAGE sql SECURITY INVOKER AS $$ UPDATE users SET locked = false $$;
exemplar.explanation: PostgreSQL runs a SECURITY DEFINER routine with the owner's (often superuser) rights; without a pinned search_path a caller can shadow built-in functions or tables and have the privileged body execute their objects (the CVE-2018-1058 class). Pinning search_path to pg_catalog (or using SECURITY INVOKER) makes the body resolve only the intended objects.
